subject: Redwood x Vectorly: hybrid storage integration and go-to-market details
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@vectorly.ai>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood x Vectorly: initial integration + pilot plan

Hi Amit —

Really excited to kick this off. As discussed in our call, Vectorly's S3-backed cold-tier combined with Redwood's in-memory KV caching looks like a compelling pattern for customers that need high recall with predictable cost.

Attached is a short deck that lays out the integration surface we propose:
- Real-time routing to Vectorly for similarity search when embeddings point to cold segments
- Native S3 fallthrough for historical vectors + transparent eviction
- A small SDK shim (Node/Python) to unify endpoints

Goals for the pilot (4–6 weeks):
1) Technical proof: index + query flow with sample dataset (5M vectors)
2) Performance targets: p50 < 75ms for cached hits, p95 < 600ms for fallthroughs
3) Co-sell GTM: joint demo + one PR blog

Ask: can you confirm technical lead at Vectorly and whether your S3 tier supports batch prefetch? We attached the draft deck for your team to annotate.

Thanks — I'll loop in Jonas and Dev for technical and GTM ops.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Marissa —

Love the outline. Quick answers and a couple of questions from our side:

1) Technical lead: I'm the PM for integrations; technical lead will be Ravi Patel (ravi@vectorly.ai) — cc'ing him on internal thread.
2) S3 support: yes — we support selective prefetch and object-level async pre-warm. We'll need to agree on TTLs and prefix heuristics.
3) Data access: for the pilot we prefer a read-only S3 role + signed URLs for prefetch. Will your SDK handle presigned flows or do we need to add one?
4) Security: we'll need a short matrix for SOC2 controls and retention. Do you have an existing questionnaire?

We'll review the deck and provide annotated notes by EOD Monday.

—Amit

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood x Vectorly: initial integration + pilot plan

Amit —

Thanks — quick technical sketch from our runtime/SE side (high level):

Redwood runtime integration points:
- Embedding evaluator -> routing layer: we tag requests with routing hints when the embedding indicates low-confidence (custom threshold)
- Cache tier: in-memory KV cache (per-host) for hot vectors, LRU with optional pinning for pinned documents
- Fallthrough: when miss, we call Vectorly's similarity API with a signed URL to fetch candidate IDs and optionally prefetch objects from S3 to local SSD before re-ranking

Sequence (simplified):
1) Client -> Redwood API (embedding)
2) Runtime checks KV cache -> hit: return
3) Miss: call Vectorly similarity endpoint (API key + session token)
4) Vectorly returns candidate vector pointers -> if object referenced is cold, request signed S3 URL for prefetch
5) Re-rank locally, return results

Notes / questions:
- Index format: we can accept ID+512-d float embeddings (float32) or quantized int8. Which does Vectorly prefer for right-now index ingestion?
- Prefetch thresholds: do you have a recommended batch size for prefetch (we've seen good perf with 64–128 objects parallelized)
- Auth: we'll support short-lived credentials (STS) and presigned GETs — fine to proceed with a role-based read-only approach.

I'll prototype a shim this week against your staging endpoint if you provide access.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
